name: ANSI panelboard plan symbol
summary: US plan symbol for a panelboard, drawn as a rectangle on the wall with fill indicating flush or surface mounting.
description: US plans draw panelboards as rectangles against the wall, with fill or hatching that distinguishes flush-mounted from surface-mounted cabinets. The panel name, such as LP-1A, is written beside it and matches the panel schedule and home-run labels.

The symbol helps coordinate wall depth for flush cabinets and working clearance in front of the panel. Readers should check that the space shown on the plan meets the required clear working space. The symbol does not show bus rating, main breaker or circuit count. These are in the panel schedule.
readingNotes: Distinguish flush and surface panels by fill.
Match the label with the panel schedule.
distinction: The IEC distribution board plan mark serves the same locating role under a different convention.
